why: A transcript is append-only history: a finding here cannot be fixed, only recorded. Each entry names a real violation of the quantified-progress rule that has already happened, so the scan can return to green without being disarmed. An entry whose finding no longer appears in a transcript this run READ fails the scan — see the header of scan-progress-report-quantification.mjs.

acknowledgments.reason: A real violation, committed by me: a mid-work audit status reported 4/6 with no percentage. History cannot be edited, so it is recorded rather than fixed.
The same violation seventeen seconds later in the same session — which is the argument for a mechanism rather than an intention, and why the rule is enforced by a scan at all.
A third instance the next day, reporting 13/16 without the percentage. Recorded for the same reason: the transcript is immutable and the alternative is a permanently red scan that gets suppressed.

A fourth instance, committed while building the acknowledgment path for the first three — reporting 78/97 of the scans still undeclared, with no percentage. Recorded rather than argued away: it is the same violation, and the fact that it happened during the fix is the clearest evidence that the rule needs a mechanism and not an intention.

A fifth instance, reporting the examined-size migration as 47/100 with no percentage while telling the owner the harness work was ending. Every instance so far has been a RATIO of a migration's progress written in a summary to the owner — which is exactly where a percentage carries the meaning and the bare fraction does not.

A sixth instance — '#1651 (CORE-027 1/3)', naming which third of an item a pull request carries. Six for six, every one a RATIO OF PROGRESS written in a summary to the owner. The rule is right and the habit is specific: it is not ratios in general that go unqualified, it is the sentence that reports how far along something is.
A real violation, committed by me: a mid-work update over a countable task set reported 19/25 with no percentage (it is 76%). History is append-only, so it is recorded rather than fixed.

Not a second violation — this message QUOTES the line above while acknowledging the rule it broke. The scan cannot tell a report from a citation of one, and widening it to try would cost more than it catches, so the citation is recorded here instead.
The same citation again, one minute later, explaining to the owner why the finding could not be fixed by a code change. Recorded for the same reason as the entry above.

Recorded rather than argued away; the scan found it on the very next run, which is the mechanism working as designed.

A real violation, committed by me: a mid-work status over three backlog items reported '1/3 완료 대기 중' with no percentage (33%). Recorded rather than fixed because the transcript is append-only. Worth noting what it cost -- the same session had just spent several gates arguing that a claim without its measurement is weaker than it reads, and the narrative reporting that argument broke the rule it was arguing for.

The message ACKNOWLEDGING the violation above committed it again, by quoting the offending ratio without the percentage. That is not a technicality: the rule is about what a reader can act on, and a quoted ratio reads exactly like an asserted one. Recorded as its own entry rather than folded into the first, because the repeat is the evidence -- an intention to comply did not survive one message.

Notable because it happened in the SAME session where I acknowledged the seventh and wrote the rule into memory, which is the argument for the scan over the intention.

A real violation, committed by me: a mid-work status table reported PEER-001 as '계약 2/4 완료' with no percentage (= 50%). Transcripts are append-only, so it is recorded rather than edited. This is the THIRD in this session — the earlier two were 6/7 ratios — which makes it a habit rather than a slip, and the correction is to state the percentage in the same breath as the ratio, not to remember afterwards.

The acknowledgement of the previous violation violated the same rule: quoting '계약 2/4 완료' while admitting it lacked a percentage still put a bare ratio in a narrative message. Recorded rather than edited, and worth keeping visible — a rule about how a number is written is broken as easily while apologising for breaking it as while reporting progress. The habit the scan is measuring is writing the ratio at all without its percentage, quotation included.
